overall.assessment: No global winner. Centrality helps concrete object/driver requests but materially regresses wealthy-people conjunction and some crime intent against strongest cheap controls. D4/fusion are not universal fallbacks. Two gated cases remain unavailable; local timings alone do not establish SQL speed.
overall.next_experiment: General clause-scoped negation plus evidence-aware conjunction and bounded anchoring; preserve control strengths without request/title-specific switches.

cases.assessment: Centrality top3 all explicitly center chases; it mostly recovers the already strong corrected list. D4/fusion promote the Universal Studios ride Fast & Furious: Supercharged (synopsis explicitly calls it a ride), a catalog mismatch. Phrase-list Black Lagoon is supported as action but supplied prose centers pirate mercenaries rather than car chases.
cases.next_experiment: Keep source centrality while preventing D4/anchor dominance from promoting ride records.
cases.evidence_basis: Actual round1 top3/top5 synopsis and essence; original six lists; no generated ranking reason treated as truth.

cases.request: I want something tense that keeps me guessing, but I don’t want to finish it feeling miserable.
cases.assessment: Caught explicitly supports suspense and twists but its ending remains unknown. New #2 Beasts Clawing at Straws explicitly has bleak atmosphere and unease, conflicting with the requested experience. New #3 Spider in the Web supports guessing but not a reassuring outcome. Earlier controls also contain bleak results; change alone is not improvement.
cases.next_experiment: Use existing negative evidence conservatively; never infer ending guarantees from missing text.
cases.evidence_basis: Actual round1 top3/top5 synopsis and essence; original six lists; no generated ranking reason treated as truth.

cases.request: Rich people being absolutely awful to each other, preferably funny.
cases.assessment: The Snake centers extortion of wealthy victims; Cartouche is a thief stealing from the rich and giving to the poor, not rich people mutually mistreating one another. Dirty Sexy Money is a direct wealth/blackmail/affairs fit, but at #3. English and fusion keep Saltburn/Gemstones/Favourite nearer the front. Centrality and coverage fail the relation despite matching rich people.
cases.next_experiment: Preserve useful combined anchors; measure relation/conjunction rather than phrase occurrence alone.
cases.evidence_basis: Actual round1 top3/top5 synopsis and essence; original six lists; no generated ranking reason treated as truth.

cases.request: A crime show that feels grubby and real. No animation, and nothing where the detective has magic powers.
cases.assessment: Centrality top3 Ten Days in the Valley / Americas Most Wanted / Vengeance Unlimited have some crime support, but first is scored by an incidental crime-show mention about its producer. English/D4/fusion put directly realistic police work in 24 Hours in Police Custody and Hidden high. Flex x Cop at #4 emphasizes wealthy comic antics, a weaker grubby-real fit. Documentary is allowed, not an error.
cases.next_experiment: Disambiguate descriptions of a show-within-the-show and retain realism evidence.
cases.evidence_basis: Actual round1 top3/top5 synopsis and essence; original six lists; no generated ranking reason treated as truth.

cases.request: Something where halfway through you realise the person telling the story has been feeding you nonsense.
cases.assessment: New top3 shift toward psychological/meta titles but do not prove a lying narrator: Twin Peaks supplied source emphasizes visions and tragic prequel, The Rehearsal staged simulations. Coverage removes Words on Bathroom Walls from #4, whose halfway-through-senior-year phrase is wrong-sense support. Moving generic ambiguity above more directly supported narrative deception is not established progress.
cases.next_experiment: Keep exact-phrase disambiguation; seek narrator-specific source evidence, not any twist.
cases.evidence_basis: Actual round1 top3/top5 synopsis and essence; original six lists; no generated ranking reason treated as truth.

cases.request: Give me car chases, but make it more getaway driver than superheroes destroying a city.
cases.assessment: Motorway/Baby Driver/Hit & Run all directly support skilled getaway driving and chases. Coverage instead puts The Refuge and Ranam high: both explicitly involve getaway drivers, so unfamiliarity is not a failure, but their supplied text supports chase centrality less than Baby Driver. D4 inserts pirate-mercenary Black Lagoon at #1, regression.
cases.next_experiment: Centrality improves conjunction over D4; do not overreward getaway noun presence without chase support.
cases.evidence_basis: Actual round1 top3/top5 synopsis and essence; original six lists; no generated ranking reason treated as truth.

cases.request: Brain’s fried. Something warm and funny, but not painfully cheesy.
cases.assessment: Here We Go and Moone Boy explicitly support warmth and comedy. Three Wise Men and a Baby adds warm holiday reconciliation; whether that feels painfully cheesy remains subjective, not a hard mismatch. Corrected already has direct warmth-comedy leaders. Fusion promoting Captain Kangaroo is a less direct adult comedy fit, though children content was not excluded.
cases.next_experiment: Record subjective uncertainty and avoid blanket family/children filtering.
